title: The Cauchy–Binet formula
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $m,n\ge0$ integers, $A$ an $m\times n$ matrix and $B$ an $n\times m$ matrix with entries in $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. For a subset $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ with $|S|=m$, let $A^{S}$ be the $m\times m$ submatrix [def-weil-submatrix] of $A$ formed by the columns with indices in $S$ and $B_S$ the $m\times m$ submatrix of $B$ formed by the rows with indices in $S$, both taken in increasing order of the indices. Then $$\det(AB)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\},\ |S|=m}\det(A^{S})\det(B_S)$$ in $R$. (For $n<m$ the sum is empty and $\det(AB)=0$; for $m=0$ both sides are $1$.)
